item.title: One Hundred Years Down, More to Go: ASALH Reflects on Centennial of Black History Month
item.description: The 100th anniversary of Black History Month is being celebrated by the Association for the Study of African American Life and History (ASALH) with a commitment to preserving and promoting the history and legacy of African Americans, despite the efforts of some to erase it. item.title: D.C. Attorney General Secured Nearly $907 Million for District in 2025: Report
item.description: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) released its 2025 Impact Report, which details a year of litigation, enforcement, and legal defense that produced $906.8 million in savings and benefits for the District, a return of more than four times the office's annual budget. item.title: Zona Maco: Navigating the Imprint of Blackness in Latin America
item.description: At Zona Maco, Black and Afro-Mexican narratives remain largely peripheral, but Sean Kelly Gallery has worked to highlight Black artists in the Mexico City market and beyond, while Magola Moreno's paintings suggest that Black presence in Latin America does not always announce itself as a category or claim. item.title: Heart Awareness Month and the Fight for Equity in Cardiac Care
item.description: Despite advances in cardiovascular care, African Americans still die at higher rates from heart disease than their white counterparts, and the Association of Black Cardiologists is working to address this disparity through initiatives such as the Cardiovascular Desert Initiative and increased education and screening programs. The post Heart Awareness Month and the Fight for Equity in Cardiac Care appeared first on The Washington Informer.
